sentences.text: Counsel contends that the petitioner was called upon to furnish the information at the time of spot inspection in respect of khasra no. 621/1 situated at village Patera District Damoh.

Counsel contends that the said information was provided and request was made by the petitioner that area in khasra no. 621/1 be corrected and 0.36 hectare be recorded in the name of petitioner and remaining 0.97 hectare be recorded in the name of Bakul Jain which falls in khasra no. 621/3.
2.
It is contended by the counsel that the land in question is now required by the Government for construction of Community Health Centre and the construction almost completed.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that in view of the subsequent events, the Collector may be directed to take decision to initiate proceedings for acquisition of the land in terms of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. Learned Deputy Advocate General for the State submits that as of now, the petitioner has not approached the Collector in terms of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013 and therefore, if the petitioner moves a representation before the Collector highlighting his grievance, the same shall be taken cognizance in accordance with law.

entities.text: Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He further contends that at this juncture, the present petition is pre-mature.

5. In view of the aforesaid, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, the present petition stands disposed of with the direction that if the petitioner prefers a representation before the Collector highlighting his grievance, as regards the acquisition of the land in question in terms of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013, then the representation shall be dealt with by the Collector by passing a well-reasoned and speaking order in accordance with law within a period of 90 days' from the date of filing of the representation alongwith certified copy of this order.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 6. It is made clear that this court has not expressed any opinion on the merit and the Collector concerned in his own wisdom shall be at liberty to deal with representation in accordance with law.

The Collector shall also be at liberty to consider the prayer of the petitioner as regards acquisition of land by mutual consent.
7.
With the aforesaid, the present petition stands disposed of.

(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE navin Dr. Neeta Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194540173/

opennyai_summary.arguments:
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that in view of the subsequent events, the Collector may be directed to take decision to initiate proceedings for acquisition of the land in terms of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013.
4. Learned Deputy Advocate General for the State submits that as of now, the petitioner has not approached the Collector in terms of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013 and therefore, if the petitioner moves a representation before the Collector highlighting his grievance, the same shall be taken cognizance in accordance with law.
He further contends that at this juncture, the present petition is pre-mature.
opennyai_summary.decision:
5. In view of the aforesaid, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, the present petition stands disposed of with the direction that if the petitioner prefers a representation before the Collector highlighting his grievance, as regards the acquisition of the land in question in terms of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013, then the representation shall be dealt with by the Collector by passing a well-reasoned and speaking order in accordance with law within a period of 90 days' from the date of filing of the representation alongwith certified copy of this order.
6. It is made clear that this court has not expressed any opinion on the merit and the Collector concerned in his own wisdom shall be at liberty to deal with representation in accordance with law.
The Collector shall also be at liberty to consider the prayer of the petitioner as regards acquisition of land by mutual consent.
7.
With the aforesaid, the present petition stands disposed of.
